questions.question: Which of the following articles of Indian Constitution is related to the Election Commission of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 324**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 324** of the Indian Constitution deals with the powers, functions, tenure, eligibility, etc., of the Election Commission of India.
 
• It provides that the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of the electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to Parliament and to the Legislature of every State and of elections to the offices of President and Vice-President held under this Constitution shall be vested in a Commission (referred to in this Constitution as the Election Commission).
 
• The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
 
• The body administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies in India, and the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India**

 
 
• The Election Commission of India was established in accordance with the Constitution on 25th January 1950.
 
• The commission has the power of superintendence, direction, and control of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President in India.
 
• It is a permanent and independent body to ensure free and fair elections in the country.
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners are appointed by the President of India. They have a tenure of six years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Articles Related to Elections in India**
 
 
• **Article 324** - Superintendence, direction, and control of elections to be vested in an Election Commission.
 
• **Article 325** - No person to be ineligible for inclusion in or to claim to be included in a special, electoral roll on grounds of religion, race, caste, or sex.
 
• **Article 326** - Elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assemblies of States to be on the basis of adult suffrage.
 
• **Article 327** - Power of Parliament to make provision with respect to elections to Legislatures.
 
• **Article 328** - Power of Legislature of a State to make provision with respect to elections to such Legislature.

questions.question:
Read the following about the Green Revolution in India.

A. The green revolution in India refers to a period when Indian Agriculture was converted into an industrial system due to the adoption of modern methods and technology such as the use of HYV seeds, tractors, irrigation facilities, pesticides and fertilizers.

B. It was funded by the US and the Indian Government and the Ford and Rockefeller Foundation.

Identify the CORRECT statement/statements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India marks a period of significant agricultural transformation in the country.
 
• This transformation was characterized by the adoption of new technologies, including High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, tractors, irrigation facilities, pesticides, and fertilizers.
 
• The revolution aimed at increasing agricultural productivity to make India self-sufficient in food grains.
 
• The initiative was financially supported by the Indian government, the United States, and international organizations such as the Ford and Rockefeller Foundations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High Yielding Variety (HYV) Seeds**

 
 
• HYV seeds are a type of seed that has been specifically bred to produce more crops per acre compared to traditional seeds.
 
• They were a key component of the Green Revolution and helped significantly increase agricultural production.
 
 
 
• **Tractors and Mechanization**
 
 
• The use of tractors and other machinery helped speed up farming processes and reduce the need for manual labor.
 
• This mechanization was crucial in transforming Indian agriculture into an industrial system.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation Facilities**
 
 
• The development and expansion of irrigation facilities ensured a more reliable water supply for crops, which is essential for high agricultural productivity.
 
• Improved irrigation helped mitigate the effects of drought and other water-related issues.
 
 
 
• **Pesticides and Fertilizers**
 
 
• The use of chemical pesticides and fertilizers helped protect crops from pests and diseases, and provided essential nutrients to the soil.
 
• These inputs were critical in achieving the high yields associated with the Green Revolution.
 
 
 
• **Ford and Rockefeller Foundations**
 
 
• These foundations played a significant role in providing financial and technical support for the Green Revolution.
 
• They helped fund research and development of new agricultural technologies and practices.

questions.question: The Green Revolution in India primarily focused on improving the production of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**wheat and rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India was initiated in the 1960s and it primarily focused on improving the agricultural production of major food grains, especially wheat and rice.
 
• This revolution led to the introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, particularly for wheat and rice, which significantly boosted the production and yield per hectare.
 
• The initiative was largely funded and supported by various international organizations, including the Rockefeller Foundation and the Ford Foundation.
 
• Dr. M.S. Swaminathan is considered as the father of the Green Revolution in India for his pivotal role in the development and introduction of these high-yielding variety seeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that occurred between the 1940s and the late 1960s, which increased agricultural production worldwide, particularly in developing countries.
 
• It involved the development and dissemination of new seed varieties, the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, and the implementation of new agricultural practices such as irrigation and mechanization.
 
• The primary goal was to achieve self-sufficiency in food grains and to combat hunger and malnutrition.
 
• Despite its success in increasing food production, the Green Revolution also led to environmental and social issues, such as soil degradation, water scarcity, and increased inequality among farmers.
 
 
 
• **High-Yielding Variety (HYV) Seeds:**
 
 
• HYV seeds are a type of seed that has been bred to produce more yield per acre than traditional varieties.
 
• These seeds are often resistant to certain diseases and pests, and they respond well to fertilizers and irrigation.
 
• The use of HYV seeds was a key component of the Green Revolution, significantly increasing the production of staple crops like wheat and rice.
 
• However, HYV seeds often require more inputs (such as water and fertilizers) and can lead to monoculture practices, which may reduce biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Dr. M.S. Swaminathan:**
 
 
• Dr. Monkombu Sambasivan Swaminathan is an Indian geneticist and international administrator, renowned for his leading role in India's Green Revolution.
 
• He is known as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India" for his work in the development of high-yielding variety seeds.
 
• Dr. Swaminathan's efforts led to significant increases in food grain production in India, helping to alleviate hunger and improve food security in the country.
 
• He has received numerous awards and honors for his contributions to agriculture and food security, including the Padma Bhushan and the Padma Vibhushan.

questions.question: When a person leaves one job (either voluntarily or involuntarily) without finding another one, they are known to be going through _______.

__
 
• **Frictional unemployment** occurs when individuals are temporarily unemployed while transitioning from one job to another.
 
• This type of unemployment is often voluntary as individuals may leave their jobs to find better opportunities or due to personal reasons.
 
• Frictional unemployment is considered a natural part of a healthy economy as it indicates that workers have the flexibility to find jobs that better match their skills and interests.
 
• This type of unemployment is usually short-term and does not indicate a fundamental problem in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disguised unemployment:**

 
 
• This occurs when more people are employed than actually needed. In other words, some workers have zero or marginal productivity.
 
• It is common in agricultural sectors where family members may work on the same plot of land but not all of them are necessary for the production output.
 
• It does not affect the overall production output and is often a characteristic of developing economies.
 
 
 
• **Cyclical unemployment:**
 
 
• This type of unemployment is related to the cyclical trends in the economy, such as the fluctuations of the business cycle.
 
• During periods of economic downturns or recessions, demand for goods and services decreases, leading to job losses.
 
• Cyclical unemployment is usually temporary and can be addressed through economic policies that stimulate demand.
 
 
 
• **Seasonal unemployment:**
 
 
• This type of unemployment occurs at certain times of the year when demand for labor in certain industries is low.
 
• It is common in industries like agriculture, tourism, and construction, where activities are dependent on seasons.
 
• Workers in these industries may be unemployed during off-seasons but find employment during peak seasons.

questions.question: The Modern Periodic Table has 18 vertical columns known as 'groups' and _______ horizontal rows known as 'periods'.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Modern Periodic Table is arranged in 7 horizontal rows called periods.
 
• Each period corresponds to the number of electron shells in the atoms of the elements in that row.
 
• The periods are numbered from 1 to 7, starting from the top to the bottom of the table.
 
• The length of each period increases as you move down the periodic table because higher periods contain more elements due to the increase in the number of available orbitals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Groups:**

 
 
• There are 18 vertical columns in the Modern Periodic Table known as groups.
 
• Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties and the same number of valence electrons.
 
• Groups are numbered from 1 to 18, starting from the leftmost column to the rightmost column of the table.
 
• Examples include Group 1 (Alkali metals), Group 2 (Alkaline earth metals), Group 17 (Halogens), and Group 18 (Noble gases).
 
 
 
• **Periods:**
 
 
• The horizontal rows in the periodic table are called periods.
 
• Each period indicates the principal energy level that is being filled with electrons.
 
• Period 1 has 2 elements (Hydrogen and Helium), Periods 2 and 3 have 8 elements each, Periods 4 and 5 have 18 elements each, and Periods 6 and 7 have 32 elements each.
 
• The properties of elements gradually change as you move across a period from left to right.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Law:**
 
 
• The Modern Periodic Table is based on the periodic law, which states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.
 
• This means that elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number, and elements with similar properties recur at regular intervals.
 
 
 
• **Electron Configuration:**
 
 
• Electron configuration refers to the distribution of electrons in the orbitals of an atom.
 
• It follows the Aufbau principle, Hund's rule, and the Pauli exclusion principle.
 
• The electron configuration of an element determines its position in the periodic table and its chemical behavior.
